questions.question: Any natural mass of mineral matter that makes up the earth's crust is __ __ .

• Earth's crust 

 
 
• Each fragment of the Earth's crust is known as a Plate.
 
• Earth consists of three parts. 
 
 
• The crust
 
• The mantle
 
• The core
 
 
 
• The Crust is the outer layer of the Earth and it is very thin compared to the core and mantle. It is made up of igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks.
 
• There are two types of crust viz oceanic and continental.
 
• The mantle lies below the crust and it is up to 2900 km thick.
 
• The core is the center of the earth.

questions.question: If we deduct depreciation from GNP the measure of aggregate income that we obtain is called __ __ .

options.text: Gross Domestic Product at market prices

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Net National Product**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Net National Product (NNP):

 
 
• NNP is obtained by subtracting depreciation value (i.e. capital stock consumption) from GNP.
 
• Net National Product (NNP) = Gross National Product − Depreciation.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP):

 
 
• It is the total money value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of the country during a given period of time.
 
• GDP = C + G + I
 
 
• C = Consumption expenditure
 
• G = Government expenditure
 
• I = Investment expenditure
 
 
 
 

 
• Gross domestic product at market prices

 
 
• Gross domestic product at market prices aims to measure the wealth created by all private and public agents in a national territory during a given period.
 
• The way of measuring GDP at market prices is the production approach as the sum of added values of all activities which produce goods and services, plus taxes and minus subsidies on products.
 
 
 
• Personal Income: 
 
 
• Income is obtained by nationals by subtracting corporate taxes and payments made for social securities provisions from national income and adding to it government transfer payments, business transfer payments and net interest paid by the government. 
 
• Personal Income = National income – undistributed profits of a corporation – payments for social security provisions – corporate tax + government transfer payments + Business transfer payments + Net interest paid by the government.

questions.question: Players that stop dribbling in handball have to pass or shot within :

• ​A player commits a **"walking" offence** if they take more than** three steps **without **dribbling, passing, or shooting the ball.**
 
• Additionally, if the player has the ball for more than** three seconds,** this may occur.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a classification of E-Commerce?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** D2D (Distributor-to-Distributor).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **B2C (Business-to-Consumer):**

 
 
• Business-to-consumer marketing describes the practice of **companies selling goods and services directly to customers **without the use of a middleman.
 
• B2C mainly refers to online merchants who use the** internet to sell goods and services to customers.**
 
 
 
• **C2C (Consumer-to-Consumer):**
 
 
• A business model known as "consumer to consumer" (C2C) allows for** private customers to deal for goods or service**s without the involvement of a business on either end of the transaction.
 
• Today, online businesses handle the **majority of C2C transactions.**
 
 
 
• **B2B (Business-to-Business):**
 
 
• Business-to-business (B2B) refers to a **deal or transaction made between two companies**, like a wholesaler and a retailer.
 
• B2B transactions typically take place in the **supply chain**, where one business buys raw materials from another in order to **utilise them in the production process.**
 
• Companies in the auto business, as well as those in** property management, housekeeping, and industrial cleanup,** frequently engage in B2B transactions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **E-commerce** is the **electronic purchase or sale of goods** through **online stores or the Internet**.
 
• E-commerce makes use of technology like **supply chain management, mobile commerce, electronic payments transfer, Internet marketing, etc.**
 
• **Online retail, electronic markets, and online auctions** are the three subfields of e-commerce.
 
• **Electronic business** provides a foundation for e-commerce.
 
• There are** five essential categories** of E-commerce:
 
 
• Business to Business
 
• Business to Consumer
 
• Business to Government
 
• Consumer to Business
 
• Consumer to Consumer

questions.question: How thick is the lithosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 to 200 kilometres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The crust and the uppermost part of the mantle are called the lithosphere. Its thickness ranges from 10-200 km. 
 
• The lithosphere is the solid, outer part of the Earth.
 
• The lithosphere includes the brittle upper portion of the mantle and the crust, the outermost layers of Earth’s structure.
 
• It is bounded by the atmosphere above and the asthenosphere (another part of the upper mantle) below.
 
• The portion of the interior beyond the crust is called the mantle.
 
• The mantle extends from Mohorovicic discontinuity to a depth of 2,900 km.
 
• The upper portion of the mantle is called Asthenosphere.
 
• It is considered to be extending up to 400 km and it is the main source of magma that finds its way to the surface during volcanic eruptions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** There are two types of lithosphere: 

 
• Oceanic lithosphere, which is associated with oceanic crust and exists in the ocean basins (mean density of about 2.9 grams per cubic centimeter)
 
• Continental lithosph ere, which is associated with continental crust (mean density of about 2.7 grams per cubic centimeter)
 
• The thickness of the lithosphere is considered to be the depth of the isotherm associated with the transition between brittle and viscous behavior.
 
• The temperature at which olivine begins to deform viscously (~1000 °C) is often used to set this isotherm because olivine is generally the weakest mineral in the upper mantle.
 
• Oceanic lithosphere is typically about 50–140 km thick (but beneath the mid-ocean ridges is no thicker than the crust), while continental lithosphere has a range in thickness from about 40 km to perhaps 280 km; the upper ~30 to ~50 km of the typical continental lithosphere is the crust.

• Under this Article, no child__ below the age of 14 years__ can be Employed to Work in any Factory or Mine Or Engaged in any other Hazardous Employment.
 
• __Punishment is 6 months to 2 years Or 5000 rupees Or Both.​__
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Nothing in Act shall apply where the child:

 
 
• Helps his family or family enterprise, which is other than any hazardous occupations or processes set forth in the Schedule, after his school hours or during vacations.
 
• Works as an artist in the audio-visual entertainment industry, including the advertisement, films, television serials or any such other entertainment or sports activities except the circus.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a natural fibre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rayon**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Natural Fibres are obtained from plants, insects and worms.
 
• Cotton, wool, linen and silk are examples of natural fibres.
 
 
• Hence Rayon is not a natural fibre.
 
 
 
• All fibres are stretched and twisted to form long threads called yarns.
 
• This is called spinning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The yarn is woven on a machine called a loom to produce fabric. 
 
 
• Cotton fibres come from the fruit of a cotton plant called a cotton boll.
 
• Woollen fibres come from the fleece of sheep, rabbits and goats.
 
• Silk fibres are obtained from the cocoon of silkworms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Synthetic fibres
 
 
• Fibres which are man-made are called synthetic fibres. Synthetic fibres are made in factories.
 
• Rayon, terrycloth, terylene, and nylon are some popular synthetic fibres.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct with reference to the election of the President of India?

options.text: He/She is indirectly elected by the elected MLAs and MPs.
The President is elected for a period of five years.
All doubts and disputes in connection with the President's election can be inquired into and decided by both the Supreme Court and High Courts.
The election takes place in accordance with the principle of proportional representation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All doubts and disputes in connection with the President's election can be inquired into and decided by both the Supreme Court and High Courts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Election of President of India:**

 
 
• **Article 54 of the Indian Constitution** specifies the criteria for **electing the president**.
 
• The elected members of both Houses of Parliament, the Legislative Assemblies of every State, the National Capital Territory of Delhi, and the Union Territory of Puducherry make up the** Electoral College** that chooses the President.
 
• **The President's tenure **in office begins on the day he assumes office and lasts for five years.
 
• A petition challenging the results of the presidential election can be filed with the Supreme Court after the vote has been counted. One voter may only cast one vote in the presidential election. 
 
• The votes of the MLAs may differ from state to state, but never those of the MPs.
 
• To maintain the balance between the State and the Union, the number of votes from MPs must match the number of votes from MLAs.** **
 
• **All MLAs **do not cast equal numbers of votes.
 
• Any MP may cast a ballot in the state capital thanks to facilities supplied by the Election Commission.
 
• Therefore, it follows from the aforementioned considerations that all MLAs' votes have equal weight.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President of India:**

 
 
• **Current President: Droupadi Murmu(since 25 July 2022)**
 
• 
 **Formation: 26 January 1950; 73 years ago**
 
 
• 
 **First holder: Rajendra Prasad**
 
 
 
 
• 
 **Vice President of India: Jagdeep Dhankhar**

questions.question: Which of the following is celebrated as the New Year in Tamil Nadu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puthandu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Tamil calendar's first day** of the year,** Puthandu **is traditionally observed as a festival by **Tamil Hindus**.
 
• The event begins on the first day of the **Tamil month of Chittirai**, according to the lunisolar Hindu calendar's solar cycle.
 
• According to the Gregorian calendar, it occurs every year on or around April 14.
 
• The traditional new year is held on the same day in other parts of South and South East Asia but is referred to by different names there, such as Vishu in Kerala and Vaisakhi or Baisakhi in central and northern India.
 
• The Tamil New Year usually occurs on April 14 of each Gregorian year, immediately after the spring equinox. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Tamils in India and Sri Lanka celebrate **Pongal**, a multi-day Hindu harvest celebration. According to the Tamil solar calendar, it is observed at the beginning of the month, and depending on the sun's orbit that particular year, the festival is typically held on January 14 or January 15.
 
• According to the Hindu calendar, **Ugadi** is New Year's Day, and it is observed in the Indian states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.
 
• **Onam **is an annual harvest festival in India that is mostly observed by Keralan Hindus. It is the official festival of the state and a significant annual event for people in Kerala, featuring a variety of cultural activities.

questions.question: In the early eleventh century, the Chola king Rajendra I built a Shiva temple and filled it with a Sun-pedestal seized from the __ __ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalukyas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the early **eleventh century, the Chola king Rajendra I** built a Shiva temple and filled it with a Sun-pedestal seized from the Chalukyas. 
 
• **Rajendra-I of the Cholas **erected a Shiva temple in the center of his kingdom and filled it with priceless statues he had taken from defeated kings, including a Sun-pedestal from the Chalukyas, a Ganesha statue, several Durga statues, a Nandi statue, an image of Bhairava and Bhairavi from the Kalingas of Orissa, and a Kali statue from the Palas of Bengal.
 
• The Chola Empire was ruled by **Rajendra Chola I from 1014** until **1044 CE**.
 
• For his role in promoting the arts, fostering trade, and greatly extending the Chola Empire, he is regarded as the most important monarch in early eleventh-century South Asia.
 
• The settlement of Mahatittha, which was later given the name Rajaraja-pura, was home to a Shiva temple built by Chola official Tali Kumaran.
 
• The island's Chola-occupied regions were given the name Mummudicholamandalam after Mummudi Chola, also known as Rajaraja I, Rajendra's father.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Palas Empire,** which arose in the Bengal region and ruled the Indian subcontinent from **750 to 1161 CE**, was a major imperial force during this time.
 
• In the middle of the third century CE, the Deccan region of India gave rise to the **Vakataka dynasty**. Their territory is thought to have spanned from the northern and southern borders of Malwa and Gujarat to the Tungabhadra River, as well as from the western and eastern borders of Chhattisgarh to the Arabian Sea. 
 
• The eastern coastal region known as **Kalinga** is typically referred to as being between the Mahanadi and the Godavari rivers, while its exact boundaries have changed over time as its rulers' territories have changed.

questions.question: Which of the following offices was NOT held by the poet Harishena?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagara-shreshthi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nagara-shreshthi **office was NOT held by the poet **Harishena**.
 
• prathama-kulika, or the chief craftsman, the nagara- shreshthi, or main banker or merchant of the city, the sarthavaha, or the head of the merchant caravans, and the head of the kayasthas, or scribes.
 
• Harishena held several positions. He was a sandhi-vigrahika, or minister of war and peace, in addition to being a **maha-danda-nayaka**, or chief judicial officer, and a Kumar-amatya, which denoted a prominent minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Samudragupta, the Gupta Emperor,** appointed **Harishena **as his court poet.
 
• The 33 lines of the Allahabad Pillar inscription, also called Prayag Prashasti, were written by Harishena.
 
• One of the key epigraphic sources to learn about the political history of the Gupta dynasty is Prayag Prashasti.
 
• Harishena was one of the many poets and academics who Samudragupta supported.

questions.question: ______ is found in association with rocks composed of calcium carbonates.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Limestone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rocks** made of **calcium carbonates or calcium and magnesium carbonates** are frequently found next to limestone. Most geological formation's sedimentary rocks include it.
 
• The primary raw ingredient for the cement industry, limestone is also necessary for the blast furnace to process iron ore.
 
• The majority of the carbonate rock in sedimentary rock, which makes **up 20% to 25%** of it, is limestone.
 
• The majority of the remaining carbonate rock is the closely related dolomite, which has a high concentration of the mineral dolomite, **CaMg(CO₃)₂**.
 
• Dolomite, limestone that has a considerable amount of dolomite (dolomitic limestone), and any other type of limestone that contains a significant amount of magnesium are all referred to as magnesia limestone, a defunct and poorly defined word. 
 
• Approximately 30% of the world's petroleum reservoirs are found in limestone rocks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The chemical element **gold** has the atomic number 79 and the symbol Au. This places it among the naturally occurring elements with higher atomic numbers.
 
• The chemical element** iron **has the atomic number 26 and the symbol Fe. It is a metal that is found in group 8 of the periodic table and the first transition series. 
 
• The atoms of diamonds are grouped in a crystal structure known as** diamond cubic**, and it is a solid form of the element carbon.
